children.title: Financial results
children.summary: This page serves as a title slide for the financial results presentation of Micron, specifically covering the second fiscal quarter (FQ2) of 2026. The visual design features a purple gradient background with a close-up image of a semiconductor wafer on the right side.

children.title: Safe harbor statement
children.summary: This page contains a 'Safe harbor statement' warning that the presentation includes forward-looking statements regarding market demand, AI impact, and financial performance which may differ from actual results. It directs readers to SEC filings (Form 10-K, 10-Q) and the company website for risk factors. The text also defines non-GAAP financial measures used in the presentation and notes that reconciliations are available in the Appendix.

children.title: Sanjay Mehrotra
children.summary: This page is a presentation slide featuring Sanjay Mehrotra, identified as the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer. The layout includes his name and title on the left side against a white background, while a professional headshot of him in a blue suit occupies the right side. The footer indicates the date March 18, 2026, and displays the Micron logo with the page number 3.

children.title: Overview (1 of 3)
children.summary: This page is the first of a three-part overview from Micron, highlighting exceptional performance in fiscal Q2 with record-breaking revenue, gross margin, EPS, and free cash flow. It notes that quarterly revenue nearly tripled compared to the previous year, with all business units reaching new highs, and provides optimistic guidance for fiscal Q3. The slide concludes by announcing a 30% increase in the quarterly dividend.

children.title: Overview (2 of 3)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Overview (2 of 3)', outlines Micron's strategic position in the AI revolution. It attributes recent results and outlook improvements to increased memory demand driven by AI, supply constraints, and strong execution. The text emphasizes that memory is a defining strategic asset for AI, enabling smarter capabilities like longer context windows and deeper reasoning, and predicts that compute architectures will become increasingly memory-intensive.

children.title: Overview (3 of 3)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Overview (3 of 3)', outlines the company's strategy regarding Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs). It explains that SCAs differ from prior Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) by offering specific multi-year commitments to improve business visibility and stability. The text highlights that these agreements provide customers with greater certainty for planning and reinforce long-term engagement across the product portfolio. Additionally, it notes the excitement over signing the first five-year SCA.

children.title: Technology (1 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Technology (1 of 2)', outlines Micron's progress in ramping up its industry-leading 1y (1-gamma) DRAM and G9 NAND technology nodes. It highlights that the 1y node is expected to become the highest-volume node in the company's history and will likely constitute a majority of their DRAM bit mix by mid-2026. Additionally, the page details plans to increase EUV (extreme ultraviolet) adoption at the 1δ (1-delta) DRAM node using latest-generation tools to optimize space efficiency and patterning.

children.title: Technology (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Technology (2 of 2)', outlines Micron's strategic outlook on NAND technology and manufacturing. It details the progress of the G9 node expected to dominate by mid-2026, plans for co-locating R&D with manufacturing in Boise and Singapore, and a commitment to increasing R&D investments in fiscal 2027 to support the AI era. The page concludes by highlighting customer recognition of Micron's quality leadership.

children.title: Data center server demand
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Data center server demand
children.summary: This slide outlines the projected demand for data center servers, highlighting that AI is driving DRAM and NAND market share to exceed 50% by calendar 2026. It notes that while traditional server demand remains robust due to agentic AI workloads and refresh cycles, both sectors are currently constrained by supply shortages of memory components. The document forecasts low-teens percentage growth in server units and continued growth in DRAM content for 2026.

children.title: Data center HBM
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Data center HBM', outlines Micron's progress and future roadmap for High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) products. It details the volume shipments of the HBM4 36GB 12H product in Q1 2026 for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, a new 16-high HBM4 sample offering 48GB capacity, and the ongoing development of the next-generation HBM4E expected to ramp in 2027.

children.title: Data center LP DRAM
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Data center LP DRAM
children.summary: This slide outlines Micron's leadership in data center LP DRAM, highlighting its power efficiency compared to DDR DRAM. It details the sampling of a 256GB LP SOCAMM2 product built on a 1y node, which enables 2TB capacity per CPU. The content also discusses the impact of AI inference growth on new architectures and mentions specific implementations like NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX at GTC.

children.title: Data center NAND
children.summary: This page outlines the growth and strategy of Micron's data center NAND business, driven by AI use cases like vector databases and KV cache offload. It highlights that Micron is in high-volume production of G9 NAND-based PCIe Gen6 SSDs, including a 122TB model with significant performance advantages over HDDs. The text reports record market share gains for the fourth consecutive year in 2025 and notes that demand significantly exceeds available supply.

children.title: PC
children.summary: This page outlines the projected impact of supply constraints on PC and smartphone unit volumes in 2026, while highlighting how on-device AI will drive memory growth. It details recent innovations in agentic AI applications like OpenClaw and specifies that PCs with these capabilities require at least 32GB of memory. Additionally, it introduces high-end personal AI workstations such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark and AMD Ryzen AI Halo, which feature 128GB configurations for running large language models.

children.title: Mobile
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's strategic position in the mobile and PC markets, highlighting recent announcements of flagship smartphones like the Samsung Galaxy S26 and Google Pixel 10. It details a significant increase in DRAM usage for flagships to nearly 80% and describes Micron's product portfolio advancements, including LPDDR5X, Gen5 QLC SSDs, and 1y-based LPDDR6 samples.

children.title: Automotive, industrial and embedded (1 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Automotive, industrial and embedded (1 of 2)
children.summary: This page outlines the performance and trends in the automotive, industrial, and embedded markets. It highlights that Total AEBU revenues reached a record high, exceeding $2 billion for the quarter. The text discusses the accelerating deployment of Level 2+ ADAS systems by OEMs and notes the significant difference in DRAM requirements between average cars (approx. 16GB) and L4 autonomous vehicles (over 300GB). Finally, it mentions Micron's technological leadership with the shipment of samples for the industry's first automotive grade 1y LPDDR5 DRAM and G9-based UFS 4.1 solution.

children.title: Automotive, industrial and embedded (2 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Automotive, industrial and embedded (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Automotive, industrial and embedded (2 of 2)', discusses the rapid growth in robotics driven by AI advancements. It highlights a projected 20-year growth vector for robotics, noting that humanoid robots will require high-end compute platforms similar to L4-capable automobiles. The text concludes by stating that Micron is well-positioned to leverage this opportunity through its technology and partnerships.

children.title: Market outlook
children.summary: This page presents a market outlook for the DRAM and NAND industries, specifically focusing on calendar 2026. It details expectations that industry bit demand will be constrained by supply due to factors like cleanroom limitations and construction lead times. The document forecasts growth in DRAM shipments (low-20s percentage range) and NAND shipments (approximately 20%), noting that Micron's supply is expected to grow in line with these industry trends.

children.title: Supply efforts (1 of 3)
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's supply efforts to address the gap between supply and demand, highlighting key manufacturing milestones. It details the acquisition of the Tongluo site from Powerchip Semiconductor for DRAM production, plans for a new cleanroom in fiscal 2026, and progress on fab construction in Idaho, New York, and Japan.

children.title: Supply efforts (2 of 3)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Supply efforts (2 of 3)', outlines the company's manufacturing and supply chain updates. It details plans to break ground on a new NAND fab in Singapore with initial output expected in late 2028, and notes that commercial shipments have begun from a new assembly and test facility in India. Additionally, it mentions that the Singapore advanced packaging facility for HBM is on track to contribute in calendar year 2027.

children.title: Supply efforts (3 of 3)
children.summary: This document page, titled 'Supply efforts (3 of 3)', outlines Micron's capital expenditure (capex) projections for fiscal years 2026 and 2027. It states that fiscal 2026 capex is expected to exceed $25 billion, driven primarily by cleanroom facility construction in Tongluo and U.S. fab projects. For fiscal 2027, the company projects a significant increase in capex to support HBM- and DRAM-related investments, with construction spending rising by over $10 billion year-over-year.

children.title: Mark Murphy
children.summary: This page is a presentation slide introducing Mark Murphy, the Chief Financial Officer. It features his name and title on the left side against a white background, while a professional headshot of him in a suit occupies the right side. The footer includes the date March 18, 2026, the Micron logo, and the page number 21.

children.title: FQ2-26 revenue
children.summary: This page displays the financial revenue for Fiscal Quarter 2 of 2026 (FQ2-26), which is reported as $23.9 billion. The slide highlights significant growth, noting that revenue increased by 75% quarter-over-quarter and 196% year-over-year. The footer indicates the date March 18, 2026, and identifies the company as Micron.

children.title: DRAM FQ2-26
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Performance by technology/DRAM FQ2-26
children.summary: The section titled 'DRAM FQ2-26' outlines the financial performance of DRAM technology for the fiscal quarter ending in 2026. It reports a revenue of $18.8 billion, which accounts for 79% of total revenue. Key metrics include a 207% year-over-year increase and a 74% quarter-over-quarter increase in revenue. Additionally, bit shipments rose by mid-single digits Q/Q, while Average Selling Prices (ASPs) increased in the mid-60s percentage range Q/Q.

children.title: NAND FQ2-26
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Performance by technology/NAND FQ2-26
children.summary: The section titled 'NAND FQ2-26' details the financial performance of the NAND technology segment for the fiscal quarter ending in 2026. It reports a revenue of $5.0 billion, which accounts for 21% of total revenue. The text highlights significant growth metrics, including a 169% year-over-year increase and an 82% quarter-over-quarter increase in revenue. Additionally, it notes that bit shipments rose by a low single-digit percentage Q/Q, while Average Selling Prices (ASPs) increased in the high-70s percentage range Q/Q.

children.title: Quarterly business unit financial results
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Quarterly business unit financial results
children.summary: The page displays a table titled 'Quarterly business unit financial results' for the company Micron, dated March 18, 2026. The table details financial performance metrics—specifically Revenue, Gross margin, and Operating margin—for four distinct business units: Cloud Memory (CMBU), Core Data Center (CDBU), Mobile and Client (MCBU), and Automotive and Embedded (AEBU). Data is presented in millions of dollars for three periods: FQ2-26, FQ1-26, and FQ2-25.

children.title: Financial performance by business unit (1 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Financial performance by business unit (1 of 2)
children.summary: This slide details the financial performance of two specific business units: Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU) and Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU). It highlights record revenues for both units, with CMBU generating $7.7 billion and CDBU generating $5.7 billion. The text also outlines significant sequential growth in revenue and gross margins for both units, attributing these increases to higher pricing, favorable mix, and cost execution.

children.title: Financial performance by business unit (2 of 2)
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Financial performance by business unit (2 of 2)
children.summary: This slide, titled 'Financial performance by business unit (2 of 2)', details the financial results for two specific business units: Mobile Client Business Unit (MCBU) and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU). It highlights record revenues for both units ($7.7 billion for MCBU and $2.7 billion for AEBU), significant sequential revenue growth driven primarily by higher pricing, and substantial improvements in gross margins.

children.title: FQ2-26 Non-GAAP operating results
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/FQ2-26 Non-GAAP operating results
children.summary: This page presents the Non-GAAP operating results for Micron's Fiscal Quarter 2 (FQ2-26), dated March 18, 2026. It lists key financial metrics including Revenue of $23.86 billion, a Gross margin of 74.9%, and Net income of $14.02 billion. The slide also details Operating expenses, Operating income, Diluted earnings per share, and Cash from operations.

children.title: Cash flow and capital allocation
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Cash flow and capital allocation
children.summary: This page outlines Micron's cash flow and capital allocation strategy from FY-23 to FQ2-26. It details financial metrics for FQ2-26, including $11.9 billion in cash flow from operations, $5.0 billion in net Capex, and $6.9 billion in adjusted free cash flow. The document also highlights shareholder returns, noting $1.4 billion spent on repurchasing 14 million shares and $1.8 billion paid in dividends.

children.title: FQ3-26 guidance Non-GAAP
children.summary: This page presents the Non-GAAP financial guidance for Micron's Fiscal Quarter 3 of 2026 (FQ3-26). It details projected metrics including Revenue ($33.5 billion ± $750 million), Gross margin (Approximately 81%), Operating expenses (Approximately $1.40 billion), and Diluted earnings per share ($19.15 ± $0.40). The slide is dated March 18, 2026.

children.title: Outlook
children.summary: This page presents the financial outlook for Micron, detailing expectations for gross margin expansion in Q3 and increased R&D investments for fiscal 2027. It outlines capital spending projections of over $25 billion for fiscal 2026, with approximately $7 billion allocated to capex in fiscal Q3 alone. The document also specifies an expected tax rate of around 15.1% for both fiscal Q3 and the full fiscal year 2026.

children.title: Financial summary
children.summary: The page displays a Non-GAAP Financial Summary table for Micron, presenting key financial metrics in millions of dollars (except per share) for fiscal quarters FQ2-26, FQ1-26, and FQ2-25. The table details Revenue, Gross margin, Operating income, Net income, Diluted earnings per share, Cash provided by operating activities, and total cash holdings. A standout value is the significant growth in revenue from $8,053 million in FQ2-25 to $23,860 million in FQ2-26.

children.title: Non-GAAP financial data and guidance
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Non-GAAP financial data and guidance
children.summary: This page presents Non-GAAP financial data and guidance for Micron, specifically detailing performance metrics for fiscal quarter 2 (FQ2-26) and providing outlooks for the next quarter (FQ3-26). The content is organized into tables covering revenue composition by product type (DRAM and NAND), sales volume changes, average selling price (ASP) changes, and key financial figures such as gross margin, operating expenses, and earnings per share. It also includes estimates for diluted shares, income tax benefits, cash from operations, and capital expenditures.

children.title: Revenue by technology
children.summary: The section titled 'Revenue by technology' presents two tables detailing financial performance across different technology segments. The first table displays revenue amounts in millions and their percentage of total revenue for the fiscal quarters FQ2-26, FQ1-26, and FQ2-25, broken down by DRAM, NAND, and Other (primarily NOR). The second table provides a comparative analysis of these same segments, showing absolute revenue figures alongside Quarter-over-Quarter (Q/Q) and Year-over-Year (Y/Y) percentage changes.

children.title: Revenue by business unit
children.path: Micron investor report 9c0becf5.pdf/Root/Revenue by business unit
children.summary: The page displays a financial table titled 'Revenue by business unit' detailing revenue figures in millions for four specific business segments: Cloud Memory (CMBU), Core Data Center (CDBU), Mobile and Client (MCBU), and Automotive and Embedded (AEBU). The data compares performance across fiscal quarters FQ2-26, FQ1-26, and FQ2-25, including quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year percentage changes. A date of March 18, 2026 is visible at the bottom left.

children.title: Consolidated results
children.summary: This section presents a series of tables detailing the Non-GAAP reconciliations for Micron's consolidated financial results. The tables reconcile GAAP figures to Non-GAAP measures across multiple periods (FQ2-26, FQ1-26, and FQ2-25), including gross margin, operating expenses, cost of goods sold, research and development, selling/general/administrative expenses, net income, income tax, adjusted EBITDA, diluted earnings per share, and adjusted free cash flow.

children.title: FQ3-26 guidance
children.summary: This section presents the FQ3-26 financial guidance, detailing Non-GAAP reconciliations. It includes a table comparing GAAP and Non-GAAP outlooks for Revenue ($33.5 billion ± $750 million), Gross margin (Approximately 81%), Operating expenses (GAAP: ~$1.60 billion vs. Non-GAAP: ~$1.40 billion), and Diluted earnings per share (GAAP: $18.90 ± $0.40 vs. Non-GAAP: $19.15 ± $0.40). A second table breaks down the specific Non-GAAP adjustments in millions, primarily consisting of stock-based compensation across cost of goods sold, R&D, and SG&A, along with tax effects.
